key_insight: Greedy best-first search finds locally equivalent graph states with fewer edges and lower maximum degree, potentially reducing quantum-state preparation costs.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing graph states can reduce CZ-gate counts and potentially circuit depth for measurement-based quantum computing and quantum repeater networks.
method: Represent graphs as search states and local complementations as transitions.
Use greedy best-first search to seek graphs with fewer edges and lower maximum degree.
Explore beyond the first local minimum to find better solutions.
evidence_signal: Experiments report improvements over integer-linear-programming and local-search approaches across random graphs, bounded-degree graphs, and most tested quantum-LDPC-derived graphs.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative gains or scaling limits, and lower maximum degree does not alone establish hardware-level circuit-depth savings.
paper_title: Optimizing Locally Equivalent Graph States in Quantum Computing Using Greedy Best-First Search
